answer: Each identity claims one cedar grove, locks a 70-credit bond, and pays a filing fee rising with each claim: the kth claim costs 31+8(k-1) credits, so the 1000th costs 8023 and 1000 fakes cost 4,027,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked bonds. Each epoch an auditor recounts falcon nests in that grove and checks each chick's quartz band against the banding registry. A band in two groves in one window proves reuse and both bonds burn, so a rented-nest ring fails: one quartz band cannot sit in two groves at once. An honest holder pays one fee, keeps one grove, and redeems the bond after a clean epoch.
